Pseudo-Frobenius numbers and defining ideals in stretched numerical semigroup ringsThanks: Key words and phrases. Numerical semigroup ring, Defining ideal, Pseudo-Frobenius number, Minimal free resolution, Stretched local ring

Do Van Kien Address: Department of Mathematics, Hanoi Pedagogical University 2, Phuc Yen, Vinh Phuc, Vietnam Email address: dovankien@hpu2.edu.vn , Naoyuki Matsuoka Address: Department of Mathematics, School of Science and Technology, Meiji University, 1-1-1 Higashi-mita, Tama-ku, Kawasaki 214-8571, Japan Email address: naomatsu@meiji.ac.jp and Taiga Ozaki Address: Department of Mathematics, School of Science and Technology, Meiji University, 1-1-1 Higashi-mita, Tama-ku, Kawasaki 214-8571, Japan Email address: ozaki0422math.meijiu@gmail.com
Abstract.

The pseudo-Frobenius numbers of a numerical semigroup HH are deeply connected to the structure of the defining ideal of its semigroup ring k⁡[H]k[H]. In this paper, we resolve a certain conjecture related to this connection under the assumption that k⁡[H]/(ta)k[H]/(t^{a}) is stretched, where aa is the multiplicity of HH. Furthermore, we provide numerical conditions for the tangent cone of k⁡[H]k[H] to be Cohen-Macaulay.

2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 13D02; Secondary 13A02, 13A30, 13G05, 20M25

1. Introduction

In commutative algebra, the study of defining ideals and free resolutions of finitely generated algebras over a field has been a fundamental area of research, as these structures contain rich information about the algebraic properties of the rings. Among the various examples studied in commutative algebra, numerical semigroup rings stand out as particularly intriguing objects due to their seemingly simple structure as one-dimensional finitely generated algebras.

Despite their simplicity, our understanding of the defining ideals of numerical semigroup rings remains surprisingly limited. For instance, Herzog [12] fully characterized the defining ideals of 3-generated numerical semigroup rings, but for semigroups with more generators, the situation becomes significantly more complex. For 4-generated semigroups, partial results have been obtained: symmetric semigroups ([3]), pseudo-symmetric semigroups ([14]), and almost symmetric semigroups ([7]). For n(≥4)n(\geq 4)-generated cases, research has primarily focused on specific classes, such as those generated by arithmetic sequences [9] or repunit numbers [2, 17], leaving a comprehensive understanding out of reach.

A deeper understanding of these defining ideals could have applications in areas such as coding theory and algebraic geometry, where numerical semigroups naturally arise. In fact, the numerical semigroup ring k⁡[H]k[H] of a numerical semigroup

H=⟨a1,a2,…,an⟩={λ1a1+λ2a2+⋯+λnan∣0≤λ1,λ2,…λn∈ℤ}H=\left<a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}\right>=\{\lambda_{1}a_{1}+\lambda_{2}a_{2}+\cdots+\lambda_{n}a_{n}\mid 0\leq\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},\ldots\lambda_{n}\in\mathbb{Z}\}

corresponds to the monomial curve C⁡(H)={(ta1,ta2,…,tan)∣t∈k}⊆knC(H)=\{(t^{a_{1}},t^{a_{2}},\ldots,t^{a_{n}})\mid t\in k\}\subseteq k^{n}, which geometrically represents a one-dimensional algebraic curve embedded in knk^{n}. The defining ideal IHI_{H} of k⁡[H]k[H] describes the defining equation of C⁡(H)C(H).

Here let us introduce the definition of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of a numerical semigroup, which plays an important role in the present paper. For a numerical semigroup HH, we put

PF⁡(H)={α∈ℤ∖H∣α+h∈H​ for all 0<h∈H}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus H\mid\alpha+h\in H\text{ for all $0<h\in H$}\}

and we call an element α∈PF⁡(H)\alpha\in\operatorname{PF}(H) a pseudo-Frobenius number of HH. The maximum integer in PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H), which is trivially equal to max⁡(ℤ∖H)\max(\mathbb{Z}\setminus H) is called the Frobenius number of HH. In the first and second authors’ previous collaborative work [11] with S. Goto and H. L. Truong, we discovered that the behavior of pseudo-Frobenius numbers of numerical semigroups could potentially describe the structure of defining ideals of their associated semigroup rings. This observation led us to the following conjecture.

Conjecture 1.1 (by discussion between the the first author, the second author, D. T. Cuong, and H. L. Truong).

Let H=⟨a1,a2,…,an⟩H=\left<a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}\right> be an nn-generated numerical semigroup. Then the following conditions are equivalent.

  1. (1)

    IH=I2⁡(f1f2⋯fng1g2⋯gn)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}f_{1}&f_{2}&\cdots&f_{n}\\ g_{1}&g_{2}&\cdots&g_{n}\end{smallmatrix}\right) for some homogeneous elements f1,f2,…,fn,g1,g2,…,gn∈S=k⁡[X1,X2,…,Xn]f_{1},f_{2},\ldots,f_{n},g_{1},g_{2},\ldots,g_{n}\in S=k[X_{1},X_{2},...,X_{n}] with positive degrees.

  2. (2)

    IH=I2⁡(X1ℓ1X2ℓ2⋯Xn−1ℓn−1XnℓnX2m2X3m3⋯XnmnX1m1)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}X_{1}^{\ell_{1}}&X_{2}^{\ell_{2}}&\cdots&X_{n-1}^{\ell_{n-1}}&X_{n}^{\ell_{n}}\\ X_{2}^{m_{2}}&X_{3}^{m_{3}}&\cdots&X_{n}^{m_{n}}&X_{1}^{m_{1}}\end{smallmatrix}\right) for some integers ℓ1,ℓ2,…,ℓn,m1,m2,…,mn>0\ell_{1},\ell_{2},\ldots,\ell_{n},m_{1},m_{2},\ldots,m_{n}>0, after suitable permutations on a1,a2,…,ana_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}.

  3. (3)

    The set PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H) forms an arithmetic sequence of length n−1n-1.

Here, I2⁡(M)\operatorname{I}_{2}(M) denotes the ideal of SS generated by 2×22\times 2 minors of a matrix MM whose entries are in SS.

While this conjecture remains unproven in its full generality, we have verified it in several important cases, including almost symmetric semigroups [11] and semigroups with maximal embedding dimension [13]. Additionally, Branco, Colaço, and Ojeda [2, 4] showed that the assertions in the conjecture are always satisfied for generalized repunit numerical semigroups, although these results were obtained independently of our conjecture.

In this paper, we prove that our conjecture holds under the assumption that k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is a stretched Artinian local ring. This condition is automatically satisfied when HH has maximal embedding dimension, making our result a significant step toward the complete resolution of the conjecture.

The structure of stretched Artinian local rings has been studied by Sally [18] for the Gorenstein case, and later extended to the general case by Elias and Valla [6], who provided a complete description of their defining ideals. However, understanding the defining ideal of k⁡[H]k[H] itself from that of k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) presents significant challenges. Our main contribution is demonstrating how these challenges can be overcome when PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H) forms an arithmetic sequence of length n−1n-1.

To state our main theorem, let us fix some notation. Let kk be a field and H=⟨a1,a2,…,an⟩H=\left<a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}\right> be a numerical semigroup, namely gcd⁡(a1,a2,…,an)=1\operatorname{gcd}(a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n})=1. We put S=k⁡[X1,X2,…,Xn]S=k[X_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n}] the polynomial ring over kk with the grading deg⁡Xi=ai\deg X_{i}=a_{i}, and consider the graded ring homomorphism φH:S→k⁡[H]\varphi_{H}:S\to k[H] defined by φ⁡(Xi)=ta1\varphi(X_{i})=t^{a_{1}} for each 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n. Let IH=Ker⁡φHI_{H}=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi_{H} be the defining ideal of k⁡[H]k[H]. For a matrix MM whose entries are in SS, I2⁡(M)\operatorname{I}_{2}(M) denotes the ideal of SS generated by 2×22\times 2 minors of MM.

Theorem 1.2.

Let H=⟨a1,a2,…,an⟩H=\left<a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}\right> be an n(≥3)n(\geq 3)-generated numerical semigroup with multiplicity a1a_{1}, and suppose that k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is stretched. Then the following are equivalent.

  1. (1)

    IH=I2⁡(f1f2⋯fng1g2⋯gn)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}f_{1}&f_{2}&\cdots&f_{n}\\ g_{1}&g_{2}&\cdots&g_{n}\end{pmatrix} for some homogeneous elements fi,gi∈Sf_{i},g_{i}\in S with positive degrees.

  2. (2)

    IH=I2⁡(X1h1X2⋯Xn−1XnX2X3⋯XnℓX1p)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}^{h_{1}}&X_{2}&\cdots&X_{n-1}&X_{n}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}&\cdots&X_{n}^{\ell}&X_{1}^{p}\end{pmatrix} for some positive integers h1,ℓ,ph_{1},\ell,p, after suitable permutations on a2,a3,…,ana_{2},a_{3},\ldots,a_{n}.

  3. (3)

    PF⁡(H)={h+α,h+2​α,…,h+(n−1)​α}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{h+\alpha,h+2\alpha,\ldots,h+(n-1)\alpha\} for some h≥0h\geq 0 and α>0\alpha>0.

When this is the case, the graded minimal SS-free resolution of k⁡[H]k[H] is given by the Eagon-Northcott complex [5] of the matrix appearing in the conditions (1) and (2).

This connection between numerical properties (pseudo-Frobenius numbers) and algebraic structures (defining ideals) is particularly interesting. It is well-known that PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H) corresponds to the degrees of generators of the graded canonical module of k⁡[H]k[H] (see [10]). This fact suggests that PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H) contains information on the ring structure of k⁡[H]k[H]. On the other hand, it is clear that the ring structure is more complicated than the numerical information in PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H) can express. In fact, the implication from (1) to (3) in Theorem 1.2 can be proven for arbitrary numerical semigroup HH, by considering the grading of the Eagon-Northcott complex ([5]). See [13, Section 2.1] for the details. Hence, if it is proven that specific patterns in PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H), such as forming an arithmetic sequence, can completely determine the structure of defining ideals, then it should be marked a significant step forward. Our result highlights how combinatorial invariants of numerical semigroups can directly inform the algebraic structure of their associated semigroup rings, assuming the stretchedness in k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}), providing a unified perspective that bridges these two areas.

The organization of this paper is as follows. In Section 2, we review basic definitions and properties of numerical semigroups, their pseudo-Frobenius numbers, and stretched Artinian local rings. Section 3 contains our main technical results, where we establish the connection between the arithmetic sequence property of PF(H) and the structure of defining ideals under the stretched condition. In Section 4, we also discuss the Cohen-Macaulay property of the associated graded ring gr​(k⁡[H])=⨁ℓ≥0𝔪ℓ/𝔪ℓ+1\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H])=\bigoplus_{\ell\geq 0}\mathfrak{m}^{\ell}/\mathfrak{m}^{\ell+1} of the graded maximal ideal 𝔪\mathfrak{m} in k⁡[H]k[H]. Section 5 consists of several examples illustrating our main theorem and discussing potential generalizations.

2. Preliminaries

In this section, the notation is defined as follows. Let HH be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by a1,a2,…,ana_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}. We always assume a1=min⁡(H∖{0})a_{1}=\min(H\setminus\{0\}), which is called the multiplicity of HH. Let kk be a field, S=k⁡[X1,X2,…,Xn]S=k[X_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n}] and V=k⁡[t]V=k[t] be the polynomial rings over kk. The numerical semigroup ring of HH, denoted by k⁡[H]k[H], is defined as

k⁡[H]=k⁡[ta1,ta2,…,tan]⊆k⁡[t].k[H]=k[t^{a_{1}},t^{a_{2}},\ldots,t^{a_{n}}]\subseteq k[t].

2.1. Fundamental notation in numerical semigroups

The Apéry set and the pseudo-Frobenius numbers are essential tools in the study of numerical semigroups. First, let us recall the definition of them.

Definition 2.1.

For 0<h∈H0<h\in H, we put

Ap⁡(H,h)={a∈H∣a−h∉H}.\operatorname{Ap}(H,h)=\{a\in H\mid a-h\notin H\}.

We put wi=min⁡{a∈H∣a≡i(modh)}w_{i}=\min\{a\in H\mid a\equiv i\pmod{h}\} for each 0≤i≤h−10\leq i\leq h-1. Then, obviously we have Ap⁡(H,h)={w0=0,w1,…,wh−1}\operatorname{Ap}(H,h)=\{w_{0}=0,w_{1},\ldots,w_{h-1}\}.

Definition 2.2.

An integer α∈ℤ∖H\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus H is called a pseudo-Frobenius number of HH, if α+h∈H\alpha+h\in H for all 0<h∈H0<h\in H. The set of all pseudo-Frobenius numbers of HH is denoted by PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H).

The following two lemmas are fundamental and used frequently.

Lemma 2.3.

[17, Proposition 2.19 (2)] For an integer z∈ℤz\in\mathbb{Z}, z∉Hz\notin H if and only if there exists α∈PF⁡(H)\alpha\in\operatorname{PF}(H) such that α−z∈H\alpha-z\in H.

Lemma 2.4.

[17, Proposition 2.20] For each 0<h∈H0<h\in H, we have

PF⁡(H)={a−h∣a∈Ap⁡(H,h) and b−a∉H for all b∈Ap⁡(H,h)∖{a}}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{a-h\mid\text{$a\in\operatorname{Ap}(H,h)$ and $b-a\notin H$ for all $b\in\operatorname{Ap}(H,h)\setminus\{a\}$}\}

Then, we have the following. Although the proof can be found in [13], let us state a brief proof for the sake of completeness.

Lemma 2.5.

[13, Lemma 2] Suppose that n≥3n\geq 3. If there are integers h≥0h\geq 0 and α>0\alpha>0 such that PF⁡(H)={h+α,h+2​α,…,h+(n−1)​α}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{h+\alpha,h+2\alpha,\ldots,h+(n-1)\alpha\}, then h∈Hh\in H and α∉H\alpha\notin H.

Proof.

First, suppose that α∈H\alpha\in H. Then (h+α)+α∈H(h+\alpha)+\alpha\in H, because α>0\alpha>0 and h+α∈PF⁡(H)h+\alpha\in\operatorname{PF}(H). However, since n≥3n\geq 3, h+2​α∉Hh+2\alpha\notin H, which is a contradiction. Hence α∉H\alpha\notin H. Then, thanks to Lemma 2.3, there exists 1≤k≤n−11\leq k\leq n-1 such that (h+k​α)−α∈H(h+k\alpha)-\alpha\in H. This implies that k=1k=1. Hence h∈Hh\in H. ∎

2.2. Stretched local rings and stretched numerical semigroup rings

The notion of stretched local rings was studied by several researchers, such as J. Sally, J. Elias, and G. Valla [6, 18]. We begin by recalling the definition of stretched Artinian local rings.

Definition 2.6 ([18]).

Let AA be an Artinian local ring with maximal ideal 𝔪\mathfrak{m}. We say that AA is stretched, if 𝔪2=(0)\mathfrak{m}^{2}=(0) or 𝔪2\mathfrak{m}^{2} is principal.

Let us review their structure theorem for stretched Artinian local rings, which is not directly used in this paper.

Theorem 2.7 ([18, Corollary 1.2] for Gorenstein case, [6, Theorem 3.1] for general case).

Let RR be an nn-dimensional regular local ring with maximal ideal 𝔫\mathfrak{n}. Let II be an 𝔫\mathfrak{n}-primary ideal of RR satisfying I⊆𝔫2I\subseteq\mathfrak{n}^{2}. Put A=R/IA=R/I and 𝔪=𝔫/I\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{n}/I. Let ℓ\ell denote the socle degree of AA, that is, ℓ\ell is the largest integer such that 𝔪ℓ≠(0)\mathfrak{m}^{\ell}\neq(0). Suppose that AA is stretched. Then we have the following.

  1. (1)

    If the Cohen-Macaulay type r⁡(A)\operatorname{r}(A) is less than n=dimRn=\dim R, then there exists a system X1,X2,…,XnX_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n} of generators of 𝔫\mathfrak{n} such that II is minimally generated by

    {Xi​Xj∣1≤i<j≤n}∪{Xj2∣2≤j≤r⁡(A)}∪{Xi2−ui​X1ℓ∣r⁡(A)+1≤i≤n}\{X_{i}X_{j}\mid 1\leq i<j\leq n\}\cup\{X_{j}^{2}\mid 2\leq j\leq\operatorname{r}(A)\}\cup\{X_{i}^{2}-u_{i}X_{1}^{\ell}\ \mid\operatorname{r}(A)+1\leq i\leq n\}

    where uiu_{i} are units in RR.

  2. (2)

    If r⁡(A)=n\operatorname{r}(A)=n, then there exists a system X1,X2,…,XnX_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n} of generators of 𝔫\mathfrak{n} such that II is minimally generated by

    {X1​Xj∣2≤j≤n}∪{Xi​Xj∣2≤i≤j≤n}∪{X1ℓ+1}.\{X_{1}X_{j}\mid 2\leq j\leq n\}\cup\{X_{i}X_{j}\mid 2\leq i\leq j\leq n\}\cup\{X_{1}^{\ell+1}\}.

We consider the condition that k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is a stretched Artinian local ring. Here, notice that, although k⁡[H]k[H] is not a local ring, k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is a local ring.

Remark 2.8.

In [18], Sally defined the stretched property for arbitrary Cohen-Macaulay local rings as follows:

A Cohen-Macaulay local ring AA with maximal ideal 𝔪\mathfrak{m} is said to be a stretched local ring, if there exists a parameter ideal QQ for AA such that QQ is a reduction of 𝔪\mathfrak{m} and A/QA/Q is a stretched Artinian local ring.

Henceforth, we can consider the condition that the local ring k⁡[[H]]k[[H]] is stretched, this is equivalent to saying that there exists f=ta1+(higher terms)f=t^{a_{1}}+\text{(higher terms)} such that k⁡[[H]]/(f)k[[H]]/(f) is a stretched Artinian local ring. However, this is not equivalent to the condition that k⁡[[H]]/(ta1)(≅k⁡[H]/(ta1))k[[H]]/(t^{a_{1}})(\cong k[H]/(t^{a_{1}})) is stretched. For example, H=⟨6,7,11,15⟩H=\left<6,7,11,15\right> satisfies that k⁡[[H]]k[[H]] is stretched but k⁡[[H]]/(t6)k[[H]]/(t^{6}) is not stretched [8].

Because the case where k⁡[[H]]k[[H]] is stretched but k⁡[[H]]/(ta1)k[[H]]/(t^{a_{1}}) is not stretched is much more complicated (cf. [8]), we concentrate on the case where k⁡[[H]]/(ta1)≅k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[[H]]/(t^{a_{1}})\cong k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is stretched in this paper.

The following lemma is the numerical criterion for stretchedness of k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) in terms of the Apéry set Ap⁡(H,a1)\operatorname{Ap}(H,a_{1}).

Lemma 2.9.

Let H=⟨a1,a2,…,an⟩H=\left<a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}\right> be a numerical semigroup with embedding dimension nn. We put ℓ=a1−n+1\ell=a_{1}-n+1. Then k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is stretched if and only if

Ap⁡(H,a1)={{0,a2,a3,…,an}(ℓ=1){0,a2,a3,…,an}∪{aλ+aμ}(ℓ=2){0,a2,a3,…,an}∪{2​aλ,3​aλ,…,ℓ​aλ}(ℓ≥3)\operatorname{Ap}(H,a_{1})=\begin{cases}\{0,a_{2},a_{3},\ldots,a_{n}\}&(\ell=1)\\ \{0,a_{2},a_{3},\ldots,a_{n}\}\cup\{a_{\lambda}+a_{\mu}\}&(\ell=2)\\ \{0,a_{2},a_{3},\ldots,a_{n}\}\cup\{2a_{\lambda},3a_{\lambda},\ldots,\ell a_{\lambda}\}&(\ell\geq 3)\end{cases}

and dimk𝔪i/𝔪i+1=1\dim_{k}\mathfrak{m}^{i}/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}=1 for all 2≤i≤ℓ2\leq i\leq\ell.

Let h∈Ap⁡(H,a1)h\in\operatorname{Ap}(H,a_{1}) such that 0≠th¯∈𝔪2/𝔪30\neq\overline{t^{h}}\in\mathfrak{m}^{2}/\mathfrak{m}^{3}. Then we can write h=aλ+aμh=a_{\lambda}+a_{\mu} for some 2≤λ≤μ≤n2\leq\lambda\leq\mu\leq n. If ℓ=2\ell=2, then 𝔪3=(0)\mathfrak{m}^{3}=(0) and

Suppose that ℓ≥3\ell\geq 3. Then 𝔪3/𝔪4≠(0)\mathfrak{m}^{3}/\mathfrak{m}^{4}\neq(0). 2.3. Defining ideals of numerical semigroup rings

The following is typically used in determining the defining ideal IHI_{H} of k⁡[H]k[H].

Proposition 2.10.

Let JJ be a graded ideal of S=k⁡[X1,X2,…,Xn]S=k[X_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n}] such that J⊆IHJ\subseteq I_{H}. If dimkS/(J+(X1))=a1\dim_{k}S/(J+(X_{1}))=a_{1}, then IH=JI_{H}=J.

Proof.

Since J+(X1)⊆IH+(X1)J+(X_{1})\subseteq I_{H}+(X_{1}) and dimkS/(J+(X1)=a1=dimkk⁡[H]/(ta1)=dimkS/(IH+(X1))CLOSE\dim_{k}S/(J+(X_{1})=a_{1}=\dim_{k}k[H]/(t^{a_{1}})=\dim_{k}S/(I_{H}+(X_{1})), we have J+(X1)=IH+(X1)J+(X_{1})=I_{H}+(X_{1}). By applying the graded Nakayama’s lemma, we conclude IH=JI_{H}=J. ∎

In this paper, the following lemma provides a method to find such JJ as in Proposition 2.10. Here, remember that deg⁡Xi=ai\deg X_{i}=a_{i} for each 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n in S=k⁡[X1,X2,…,Xn]S=k[X_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n}].

Lemma 2.11.

Let f1,f2,g1,g2∈S+f_{1},f_{2},g_{1},g_{2}\in S_{+} be monomials in X1,X2,…,XnX_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n}. Then f1​g2−f2​g1∈IHf_{1}g_{2}-f_{2}g_{1}\in I_{H} if and only if deg⁡g1−deg⁡f1=deg⁡g2−deg⁡f2\deg g_{1}-\deg f_{1}=\deg g_{2}-\deg f_{2}.

Proof.

    IH=I2⁡(X1h1+1X2⋯Xn−1XnX2X3⋯XnℓX1h1+1+αℓ)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}^{h_{1}+1}&X_{2}&\cdots&X_{n-1}&X_{n}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}&\cdots&X_{n}^{\ell}&X_{1}^{\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}}\end{pmatrix}, where a1=aa_{1}=a, an=ba_{n}=b, and ai=h+(i−1)​α+aa_{i}=h+(i-1)\alpha+a for 2≤i≤n−12\leq i\leq n-1.

Proof.

(1) Since gcd⁡(a,b)=1\operatorname{gcd}(a,b)=1 by Lemma 3.5, the sets {0,b,2​b,…,ℓ​b}∪{ℓ​b−α,ℓ​b−2​α,…,ℓ​b−(n−2)​α}\{0,b,2b,\ldots,\ell b\}\cup\{\ell b-\alpha,\ell b-2\alpha,\ldots,\ell b-(n-2)\alpha\} and {0,b,2​b,…,(ℓ+n−2)​b}\{0,b,2b,\ldots,(\ell+n-2)b\} are complete systems of representatives modulo aa. Using similar considerations as in the proof of Theorem 3.6, we have b≡−α(moda)b\equiv-\alpha\pmod{a}.

(2) + (3) Since ℓ​b=h+(n−1)​α+a≡−ℓ​α(moda)\ell b=h+(n-1)\alpha+a\equiv-\ell\alpha\pmod{a}, we have h+(n+ℓ−1)​α+a≡h≡0(moda)h+(n+\ell-1)\alpha+a\equiv h\equiv 0\pmod{a} (Notice that n+ℓ−1=an+\ell-1=a). Thus, we can write h=h1​ah=h_{1}a for some h1≥0h_{1}\geq 0.

Now, observe that ℓ⁡(b+α)=(h1+1)​a+(ℓ+n−1)​α=(h1+1+α)​a\ell(b+\alpha)=(h_{1}+1)a+(\ell+n-1)\alpha=(h_{1}+1+\alpha)a. Therefore

b+αa=ℓ⁡(b+α)ℓ​a=h1+1+αℓ.\frac{b+\alpha}{a}=\frac{\ell(b+\alpha)}{\ell a}=\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}.

(4) By a similar computation as in the proof of Theorem 3.6, we obtain

IH=I2⁡(X1h1+1X2⋯Xn−1XnX2X3⋯XnℓX1h1+1+αℓ).I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}^{h_{1}+1}&X_{2}&\cdots&X_{n-1}&X_{n}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}&\cdots&X_{n}^{\ell}&X_{1}^{\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}}\end{pmatrix}.

∎

4. Cohen-Macaulayness of gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H])

In this section, we explore the Cohen-Macaulay property of the tangent cone gr​(k⁡[H])=⨁n≥0𝔪n/𝔪n+1\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H])=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathfrak{m}^{n}/\mathfrak{m}^{n+1} of the numerical semigroup ring k⁡[H]k[H], when k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is stretched, where 𝔪\mathfrak{m} denotes the graded maximal ideal of k⁡[H]k[H].

Throughout this section, let HH be a numerical semigroup satisfying the condition in Theorem 3.6 or Theorem 3.7. In each case, 𝔪ℓ+1⊆(ta1)\mathfrak{m}^{\ell+1}\subseteq(t^{a_{1}}) and 𝔪ℓ⊈(ta1)\mathfrak{m}^{\ell}\not\subseteq(t^{a_{1}}). Therefore, it is known by [18, Corollary 2.4] that gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if t(ℓ+1)​b∈ta1​𝔪ℓt^{(\ell+1)b}\in t^{a_{1}}\mathfrak{m}^{\ell}. Notice that, k⁡[H]≅k⁡[X1,X2,…,Xn]/IHk[H]\cong k[X_{1},X_{2},\ldots,X_{n}]/I_{H} where IHI_{H} is the same form as in Theorem 3.6 (resp. Theorem 3.7) when j=1j=1 (resp. j=n−1j=n-1).

Theorem 4.1.

Under the notation as in Theorem 3.6, gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if h1+1≥ℓh_{1}+1\geq\ell.

Proof.

By considering the form of the defining ideal given in Theorem 3.6, we immediately get that (ℓ+1)​b=(h1+1)​a1+a3(\ell+1)b=(h_{1}+1)a_{1}+a_{3}. Furthermore, we know that there are no other expressions of (ℓ+1)​b(\ell+1)b in HH by the form of the defining ideal again. Therefore, t(ℓ+1)​b−a=th1​a1+a3∈𝔪ℓt^{(\ell+1)b-a}=t^{h_{1}a_{1}+a_{3}}\in\mathfrak{m}^{\ell} if and only if h1+1≥ℓh_{1}+1\geq\ell. ∎

Theorem 4.2.

Under the notation as in Theorem 3.7, we have the following.

  1. (1)

    gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if h1+1+αℓ≥ℓ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\geq\ell.

  2. (2)

    If h1≥ℓ2−ℓ−αh_{1}\geq\ell^{2}-\ell-\alpha, then gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay.

  3. (3)

    If ℓ=2\ell=2, then gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay.

Proof.

(1) By Theorem 3.7, we have (ℓ+1)​b=h1+1+αℓ​a1+an−1(\ell+1)b=\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}a_{1}+a_{n-1}. We may even find other expressions by using the relation X1h1+1​Xn−1≡X2​Xn−2​mod​IHX_{1}^{h_{1}+1}X_{n-1}\equiv X_{2}X_{n-2}\mathrm{mod}I_{H}, the total degree of the left-hand side is greater than or equal to that of the right-hand side. Hence, t(ℓ+1)​b−a∈𝔪ℓt^{(\ell+1)b-a}\in\mathfrak{m}^{\ell} if and only if h1+1+αℓ≥ℓ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\geq\ell.

(2) Suppose h1≥ℓ2−ℓ−αh_{1}\geq\ell^{2}-\ell-\alpha. Then h1+1+α≥ℓ⁡(ℓ−1)+1h_{1}+1+\alpha\geq\ell(\ell-1)+1. Since h1+1+αℓ∈ℤ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\in\mathbb{Z}, it is at least ℓ\ell. Therefore, in this case, gr​(k​[[H]])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[[H]]) is Cohen-Macaulay thanks to (1).

(3) If h1≥1h_{1}\geq 1, then h1+1+α≥3h_{1}+1+\alpha\geq 3. Hence, since ℓ=2\ell=2 and h1+1+αℓ∈ℤ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\in\mathbb{Z}, we have h1+1+αℓ≥2=ℓ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\geq 2=\ell. By (1), we conclude that gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay.

On the other hand, suppose h1=0h_{1}=0. If α=1\alpha=1, then an=a+(n−1)2<aa_{n}=\frac{a+(n-1)}{2}<a. However, it is impossible because we assume that aa is the multiplicity of HH. Hence α≥2\alpha\geq 2. Then h1+1+α=1+α≥3h_{1}+1+\alpha=1+\alpha\geq 3 and this is even. Hence h1+1+αℓ≥2=ℓ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\geq 2=\ell. Hence gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay again by (1). ∎

Corollary 4.3.

Under the notation as in Proposition 3.4, we further assume that HH has almost maximal embedding dimension, that is, ℓ=2\ell=2. Then gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is NOT Cohen-Macaulay if and only if j=1j=1 and h=b=a+αh=b=a+\alpha.

5. Examples

In the last section of this paper, we guarantee that examples satisfying the assumptions of our results exist by providing concrete examples. In this section, kk denotes an arbitrary field the same as in previous sections.

Example 5.1.

Let ℓ≥2\ell\geq 2, n≥3n\geq 3, α>0\alpha>0, and h1≥0h_{1}\geq 0 be integers. Put a=ℓ+n−1a=\ell+n-1 and assume that gcd⁡(a,α)>1\operatorname{gcd}(a,\alpha)>1.

  1. (1)

    Let b=(h1+1)​a+αb=(h_{1}+1)a+\alpha. Then, the numerical semigroup

    H=⟨a,b,ℓ​b+α,ℓ​b+2​α,…,ℓ​b+(n−2)​α⟩H=\langle a,b,\ell b+\alpha,\ell b+2\alpha,\ldots,\ell b+(n-2)\alpha\rangle

    satisfies the assumptions of Theorem 3.6.

  2. (2)

    Suppose that h1+1+αℓ∈ℤ\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}\in\mathbb{Z} and h1+1+αℓ​a−α>a\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}a-\alpha>a. Let b=h1+1+αℓ​a−αb=\frac{h_{1}+1+\alpha}{\ell}a-\alpha. Then, the numerical semigroup

    H=⟨a,ℓ​b−(n−2)​α,ℓ​b−(n−3)​α,…,ℓ​b−α,b⟩H=\langle a,\ell b-(n-2)\alpha,\ell b-(n-3)\alpha,\ldots,\ell b-\alpha,b\rangle

    satisfies the assumptions of Theorem 3.7.

Example 5.2.

Let H=⟨a1=6,a2=13,a3=40,a4=41⟩H=\left<a_{1}=6,a_{2}=13,a_{3}=40,a_{4}=41\right>, which is the case (1) of Example 5.1 where ℓ=3\ell=3, n=4n=4, α=1\alpha=1, and h1=1h_{1}=1. Then we have the following.

  1. (1)

    Ap⁡(H,6)={0,13,40,41}∪{26,39}\operatorname{Ap}(H,6)=\{0,13,40,41\}\cup\{26,39\}. Hence k⁡[H]/(t6)k[H]/(t^{6}) is stretched.

  2. (2)

    PF⁡(H)={33,34,35}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{33,34,35\}.

  3. (3)

    IH=I2⁡(X12X23X3X4X2X3X4X17)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}^{2}&X_{2}^{3}&X_{3}&X_{4}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{1}^{7}\end{pmatrix}.

  4. (4)

    Since h1+1=1<3=ℓh_{1}+1=1<3=\ell, gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is not Cohen-Macaulay by Theorem 4.1.

Example 5.3.

Let H=⟨a1=7,a2=39,a3=43,a4=47,a5=17⟩H=\left<a_{1}=7,a_{2}=39,a_{3}=43,a_{4}=47,a_{5}=17\right>, which is the case (2) of Example 5.1 where ℓ=3\ell=3, n=5n=5, α=4\alpha=4, and h1=4h_{1}=4. Then we have the following.

  1. (1)

    Ap⁡(H,7)={0,39,43,47,17}∪{34,51}\operatorname{Ap}(H,7)=\{0,39,43,47,17\}\cup\{34,51\}. Hence k⁡[H]/(t7)k[H]/(t^{7}) is stretched.

  2. (2)

    PF⁡(H)={32,36,40,44}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{32,36,40,44\}.

  3. (3)

    IH=I2⁡(X15X2X3X4X5X2X3X4X53X13)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}^{5}&X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{5}\\ X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{5}^{3}&X_{1}^{3}\end{pmatrix}.

  4. (4)

    Since h1=4>2=ℓ2−ℓ−αh_{1}=4>2=\ell^{2}-\ell-\alpha, gr​(k​[H])\mbox{\rm gr}(k[H]) is Cohen-Macaulay by Theorem 4.2.

The following example says that the condition ♯​PF⁡(H)=n−1\sharp\operatorname{PF}(H)=n-1 can not be removed from our argument.

Example 5.4 ([11]).

Let H=⟨a1=6,a2=11,a3=13,a4=16,a5=20⟩H=\left<a_{1}=6,a_{2}=11,a_{3}=13,a_{4}=16,a_{5}=20\right>. Then Ap⁡(H,6)={0,11,13,16,20}∪{27}\operatorname{Ap}(H,6)=\{0,11,13,16,20\}\cup\{27\}. This also implies by Lemma 2.9 that k⁡[H]/(t6)k[H]/(t^{6}) is stretched. We have PF⁡(H)={7,14,21}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{7,14,21\}, whence HH does not satisfy the condition (3) in Theorem 1.2 because it is an arithmetic sequence of length 3≠5−13\neq 5-1. Therefore the defining ideal IHI_{H} of k⁡[H]k[H] can not have the form as in the condition (2). In fact, a direct computation gives

IH=I2​(X3X13X5X12​X2X2​X4X1X2X3X4X5)+(X22−X1​X4,X42−X12​X5).I_{H}=\mathrm{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{3}&X_{1}^{3}&X_{5}&X_{1}^{2}X_{2}&X_{2}X_{4}\\ X_{1}&X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{5}\end{pmatrix}+(X_{2}^{2}-X_{1}X_{4},X_{4}^{2}-X_{1}^{2}X_{5}).

Remember that the assumption that IHI_{H} is generated by 2×22\times 2 minors of a 2×n2\times n matrix implies ♯​PF⁡(H)=n−1\sharp\operatorname{PF}(H)=n-1.

The next example shows how the condition that k⁡[H]/(ta1)k[H]/(t^{a_{1}}) is stretched gives a strong restriction on the defining ideals IHI_{H}, and also demonstrates that IHI_{H} certainly does not have the desired system of generators when PF⁡(H)\operatorname{PF}(H) does not form an arithmetic sequence, even if ♯​PF⁡(H)=n−1\sharp\operatorname{PF}(H)=n-1.

    J=(X25,X2​X3,X2​X4,X2​X5,X32,X3​X4,X3​X5,X42,X4​X5,X52).J=(X_{2}^{5},X_{2}X_{3},X_{2}X_{4},X_{2}X_{5},X_{3}^{2},X_{3}X_{4},X_{3}X_{5},X_{4}^{2},X_{4}X_{5},X_{5}^{2}).

Furthermore, it can be expressed as follows by using the matrix representation:

    IH=I2⁡(X1X24X3X4X5X2X4X14X5X1​X3)+I2⁡(X13X2X3X4X5X3X12X5X1​X24X25)I_{H}=\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}&X_{2}^{4}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{5}\\ X_{2}&X_{4}&X_{1}^{4}&X_{5}&X_{1}X_{3}\end{pmatrix}+\operatorname{I}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}X_{1}^{3}&X_{2}&X_{3}&X_{4}&X_{5}\\ X_{3}&X_{1}^{2}&X_{5}&X_{1}X_{2}^{4}&X_{2}^{5}\end{pmatrix}

    PF⁡(H)={10,11,12,13}\operatorname{PF}(H)=\{10,11,12,13\}.
